extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent attorneys/agents, draftsmen, and applicants preparing patent application drawings for submission to the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare drawings for U.S. patent applications in compliance with 37 C.F.R. §1.84, covering format, medium, sizing, margins, numbering, quality, views, reference characters, symbols, and common rejection causes. Applies to both utility and design applications (with some distinctions for color and broken lines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing format and medium (black & white; color allowances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Black and white drawings are normally required, using India ink or its equivalent that secures solid black lines. Color drawings are permitted in design applications, and on rare occasions, color drawings may be necessary as the only practical medium in utility patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color drawings when used must be of sufficient quality such that all details are reproducible in black and white in the printed patent. India ink or equivalent that produces solid black lines is expected for ordinary submissions; avoid media that produce gray, washed-out, or uneven lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs (when permitted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs are not ordinarily permitted in utility and design patent applications, but the Office will accept photographs if they are the only practicable medium for illustrating the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted examples include electrophoresis gels, blots, autoradiographs, cell cultures, histological tissue sections, animals, plants, in vivo imaging, and thin layer chromatography plates. Photographs require justification that they are the only practicable medium; otherwise they may lead to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and identifying indicia
rubrics_metrics.description: Each sheet must include identifying indicia placed on the front of each sheet within the top margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required identifying indicia: title of the invention; inventor's name; application number or docket number. Ensure these items appear in the top margin on the front of every sheet to avoid procedural defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper size
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved sheet sizes: A4 (21.0 cm × 29.7 cm) or 8.5" × 11".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use one of these standard sizes for every drawing sheet to meet Office requirements and avoid rejection for improper sheet dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins (minimum)
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum margins required on each sheet: 2.5 cm top, 2.5 cm left, 1.5 cm right, 1.0 cm bottom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain these clear margins to allow for binding, printing, and placement of identifying indicia. Incorrect margins are a common cause of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheet numbering format
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheet numbering must be two Arabic numerals separated by an oblique (fraction-like) line, e.g., "1/4", "2/4".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number every sheet in this format (sheet number/total sheets). Improper numbering format can lead to procedural objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures must be numbered with consecutive Arabic numerals starting at 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number figures sequentially (1, 2, 3, ...). Use these same figure numbers consistently in the specification and drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing quality (linework and reproducibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines must be black, well-defined, uniform in thickness, sharp without blurring or jagged edges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use solid black lines for claimed features and ensure overall quality sufficient for reproduction at 2/3 size. Avoid light, broken, or uneven lines; insufficient quality (blurry, light, broken lines) is a common rejection reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of solid and broken lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Solid lines are used for claimed features; broken lines are used for unclaimed environment (in design patents) or hidden features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply solid vs. broken lines consistently and according to whether the element is claimed. Misuse leads to ambiguity and potential rejection, especially in design practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Views and figures completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Include sufficient views to show the invention completely; provide one view suitable for inclusion on the front page. Use cross-sectional, perspective, exploded views as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select views that fully disclose the claimed subject matter. Ensure reference characters are consistent across views. Failure to show the invention completely or to include a suitable front-page view can impede application processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead lines and reference numerals
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide lead lines for each reference numeral; reference numerals must be not less than 0.32 cm (1/8") in height; the same parts in different views must use the same reference characters; reference characters must appear in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every reference numeral has a clear lead line pointing to the feature. Maintain minimum text size for legibility and cross-reference every numeral in the specification. Missing reference numerals or inconsistent reference characters between views and the description are frequent rejection reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols and hatching
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard graphical symbols (electrical, hydraulic, etc.) and cross-hatching to distinguish materials; employ specific patterns for different material types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply conventional symbol standards and consistent hatching patterns so materials and systems are unambiguous. Nonstandard or inconsistent symbols/hatching may reduce clarity and lead to examiner objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common drawing rejection reasons (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent causes for drawing rejection include insufficient quality (blurry, light, broken lines); missing reference numerals; incorrect margins or numbering; color used without petition; photographs without justification; inconsistent reference characters between views and description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this list as a checklist to avoid predictable rejections: verify line quality, presence and legibility of numerals, conformity to margin and numbering rules, proper authorization/justification for color or photographs, and consistency of reference characters across drawings and text.
